title: USTC: Earth Sciences and the Xingyun Poetry Club
dek: B.S. with Honors in Geological and Earth Sciences at the University of Science and Technology of China.
narrative: Koutian Wu entered USTC in Hefei in 2020, majoring in Geological and Earth Sciences. The undergraduate years included field trips, observational atmospheric work with the Mengcheng meteor radar group, and the science writing that produced his first peer-reviewed papers.

Outside the lab, he founded and led the USTC Student Xingyun Poetry Club, becoming the second-youngest student club president in USTC history at age 17 and growing the club to over 1,197 members and 25+ cultural events. The poetry-club arc and the science arc ran in parallel — both publicly trackable, both anchored at USTC.
proofPoints: Wu, K., Yi, W., Xue, X., Reid, I. M., & Lu, M. (2024). Diurnal and seasonal variations of meteor speed and arrival angle observed by Mengcheng meteor radar. JGR: Space Physics.
Wu, K., Xu, X., Jiang, J., & Shen, A. (2024). A summary report on the Space Physics practical education in 2022. Reviews of Geophysics and Planetary Physics.

title: Shenzhen X-Institute Fellowship: from directionless to interdisciplinary
dek: Student Fellow at the Shenzhen X-Institute, a talent program jointly founded by the Shenzhen Municipal Government and Tsinghua University.
narrative: Concurrent with USTC, Wu spent more than two years (October 2021 – February 2024) as a Student Fellow at the Shenzhen X-Institute, a Shenzhen Municipal Government / Tsinghua University talent development program.

The People's Daily Overseas Edition profile (May 28, 2025) framed this period as the turning point — the move from feeling directionless as an undergraduate to picking an interdisciplinary research path. Tsinghua University's news portal subsequently republished the same piece.
proofPoints: People's Daily (Overseas Edition), May 28, 2025: 从'零'到'一' 破界创新（学创天地）

title: Visiting Scholar at NSF NCAR: Hunga–Tonga in the MLT region
dek: Six months at the U.S. National Center for Atmospheric Research, working with the WACCM-X group.
narrative: From July to December 2023, Wu was a Visiting Scholar at NSF NCAR in Boulder, Colorado. He worked with Han-Li Liu's WACCM-X group, combining global model output with meteor radar observations to investigate how the January 2022 Hunga–Tonga eruption perturbed the Mesosphere–Lower Thermosphere region.
The work was presented as AGU Fall Meeting abstract SA33B-2892 (2023). The Boulder period also seeded the relationships and modeling familiarity that later shaped the UT Austin PhD.
proofPoints: Wu, K., Liu, H.-L., Yi, W., & Xue, X. (2023). Perturbations by the 2022 Hunga-Tonga Volcano Eruption in the MLT Region Investigated Using the WACCM-X Simulation and Meteor Radar Observations. AGU Fall Meeting Abstracts, SA33B-2892.

title: Industry side-quest: AI agents and full-stack LLM
dek: Two 2025 internships bridging research and production AI.
narrative: Alongside the early UT Austin PhD chapter (started Aug 2024), Wu took two 2025 industry roles. He worked as an AI Agent Evaluation Engineer at PineAI and as a Full-Stack LLM Developer at Beijing ZaiwenAI Technology Co., Ltd.

These roles fed directly into the way he later approached land surface modeling — the 'AI for science' framing on the doctoral side did not come from a textbook, it came from shipping LLM systems and evaluating agents at scale.

title: UT Austin PhD: AI for Noah-MP land surface modeling
dek: Doctoral work at the Jackson School of Geosciences with advisor Zong-Liang Yang.
narrative: Wu joined the Jackson School of Geosciences as a Graduate Research Assistant in August 2024, with a concurrent 2024–2025 Graduate Teaching Assistant appointment at UT Austin. His doctoral focus is model optimization of physics-based land surface models, including Noah-MP, CTSM, and HRLDAS, with explainable AI and machine learning integrated to improve plant–rock–water interaction simulation.

He is the Project Administrator for NSF NCAR allocation UTAA0012, 'Explainable AI for Improving Physics-Based Noah-MP Land Surface Modeling of Plant–Rock–Water Interactions,' which has received a significant HPC allocation on the NSF NCAR Derecho-GPU supercomputer.

First-author conference work from this chapter: Wu, K., Li, L., Rempe, D., Matheny, A. M., Mbarak, M., & Yang, Z.-L. (2026). How Does Integrating Plant Hydraulics Improve Noah-MP Land Surface Model. 106th AMS Annual Meeting.
proofPoints: AMS 2026 abstract: How Does Integrating Plant Hydraulics Improve Noah-MP Land Surface Model

title: AI for land surface modeling, with HPC at scale
dek: The current research direction: explainable AI inside physics-based Earth system models, running on Derecho-GPU.
narrative: The current chapter is not a CV summary — it is a working research program. The thesis is that AI and physics-based modeling are not substitutes; the leverage is in using explainable AI to improve where Noah-MP gets plant–rock–water interactions wrong, then sending the upgraded physics back through the broader land–climate workflow.

Day-to-day, that means HPC runs on NSF NCAR's Derecho-GPU supercomputer under allocation UTAA0012, joint work with Zong-Liang Yang, Daniella Rempe, and Ashley Matheny at UT Austin, and a publication trajectory that started at AMS 2026 and is aiming further out from there.
